reason: A is a robust single file with zero axe violations, correct keyboard/focus behaviour and an honest local sign-up that never claims a send, with every sample labelled; its defects (long-email overflow at 390, Escape not closing the menu, post-click disclosure) are small fixes. B is well-engineered in places (skip link, per-field errors, reduced-motion handling) but its primary action mails an address the brief never supplied and it presents invented agenda, volunteers and coverage as real. I would change my mind only if the client had supplied alerts@commonread.org and the Linden Falls pilot details.
